To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a method to control the stiffness and torque of a soft- actuator independently and that this method is applied to an exoskeleton to assist a person during walking.

the proposed approach allows to adapt torque and stiffness of the actuator independently, that the actuator is capable of performing a wide range of motion tasks, and that the actuator can be used for safe and human- like HRI.

(1) the proposed approach is capable to independently adjust torque as well as stiffness of a direct rotary pneumatic soft-actuator, and (2) the proposed approach allows for a simple and intuitive adaptation of the actuator characteristics for different tasks and/or persons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of control strategies to adapt the output characteristics of a soft- actuator for HRI applications.
the development of an actuator system with adjustable compliance and torque for HRI applications.
the design and development of a pneumatic REC actuator for HRI and its control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a direct rotary soft- actuator can be used for human robot interaction, if it has the ability to adjust the torque and stiffness independently.
the presented actuator concept is a suitable and promising approach for HRI applications.
the presented approach is suitable to independently adjust the torque and the stiffness of the REC and thus to control both properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented approach is a first step towards the realization of a soft-robotic exoskeleton with adaptable HRI properties.
the presented actuator concept is suitable for HRI applications due to inherent compliance, high power-to-weight ratio, and independent torque and stiffness adjustment.
the presented approach allows to adapt the actuation characteristics to the specific needs of HRI and to improve the overall system performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by adjusting the stiffness and torque independently, it is possible to adapt the actuation characteristics for various HRI scenarios.
the actuator output torque can be controlled by adjusting the pressure of the actuator chambers, while the stiffness can be controlled independently by adjusting the actuator chamber geometry.
it is possible to achieve independent adjustment of torque and stiffness of a soft- actuator with direct acting REC, which is not possible with conventional pneumatic muscles.
